To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the exchange rate policies in most non European Mediterranean countries are not very different from the exchange rate policies followed by the benchmark countries and that the credibility of these policies, as assessed by the market, is not very different from that of the benchmark countries either.

i) the exchange rate regimes of the seven non European Mediterranean economies are characterized by a moderate degree of fundamental volatility and a moderate degree of market credibility; ii) there is a significant degree of market credibility for the exchange rate management in Egypt and Turkey; iii) there are significant differences in the exchange rate management between the European non EU countries, on the one hand, and the Mediterranean countries on the other.

, in general, the Mediterranean countries have a relatively credible and stable monetary policy.
the exchange rate management in the Mediterranean countries is quite moderate.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the exchange rate management is not a major concern of the foreign exchange markets.
the exchange rate policies in these countries are generally quite credible and that the foreign exchange markets are generally quite stable.

the exchange rate policies in the Mediterranean countries are not as bad as often claimed in the literature and that the exchange rate volatility in these markets is comparable to the volatility of exchange rates in the European non eu countries.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the credibility of the exchange rate management in these Mediterranean countries is not a serious issue, and that the main concern is that the fundamental exchange rate volatility is quite high in most of these countries, suggesting that exchange rate policy should be aimed at lowering the fundamental volatility of exchange rates in these countries.
exchange rate management in the countries under scrutiny is quite effective in stabilizing exchange rate fluctuations.

the exchange rate management in the countries under consideration is characterized by a moderate degree of exchange rate volatility that is consistent with a relatively moderate degree of exchange market intervention.
